description: Generate a slide-deck-quality decision tree drawn left to right in clean columns of rounded boxes, in the decision-analysis convention: a square where a decision splits into options, a circle where chance splits into events, and a triangle at each end outcome. Branch lines carry an optional `label` ("Yes", "No", an option) and, under a chance node, the probability ("Strong demand · 60%"); end outcomes can carry a numeric `payoff`, lined up in a column at the right (`prefix` "$", `suffix` "m"). Expected values are rolled back automatically once the tree has payoffs and probabilities: every decision and chance node shows its EV, each decision's best option is drawn in the accent colour and the rejected ones are muted with a ‖ prune mark; probabilities that don't add up to 100% are warned about and drawn as given. Node types are inferred (branches with probabilities make a chance node, no branches an outcome, otherwise a decision), so a plain yes/no troubleshooting or eligibility flowchart is just questions with "Yes"/"No" labels and no numbers. Choose it for choosing between options under uncertainty (launch, invest, build vs buy, litigate or settle), expected-value and decision-analysis homework, and yes/no question flowcharts; use an issue tree instead to break a problem or metric into its parts, a chevron process for steps in order, and a Harvey ball matrix to score options against criteria. Limits: 5 levels including the root, up to 5 branches per node, 40 nodes; keep names to a few words. Infer missing details rather than asking; the user can adjust the chart in the builder through the Edit link. ALWAYS give the user the image link: inline chat images usually cannot be saved, but the link renders the exact chart on demand and can be pasted into a slide or Markdown.

node.description: One node in the tree: a decision, a chance event or an end outcome. Its children are the branches leaving it.

children.description: The branches leaving this node, top to bottom (up to 5): the options of a decision, the possible events of a chance node, or the answers to a question.

label.description: Optional text on the branch line leading into this node, e.g. "Yes" / "No" in a question flowchart, or an option name. Under a chance node it is followed by the probability ("Strong demand · 60%"). Omit it when the node's name already says it.

name.description: The text in the node's box: the decision or question ("Launch Atlas?", "Is the router on?"), the option or event it stands for ("Launch now", "Strong demand"), or the end result ("Replace the cable"). Wraps onto three lines, then truncates; keep it to a few words.

payoff.description: Optional value of an end outcome as a plain number (4.2 for $4.2m with prefix "$" and suffix "m"; negative for a loss). Shown right-aligned in a payoff column at the right edge and used to roll back expected values. Only counts on nodes without children.

probability.description: Optional probability of this branch, for children of a chance node. Write it as 0–1 (0.6) or as a percentage (60): any value above 1 is read as a percentage, so write 1% as 0.01. Drawn on the branch as "60%". Branches of a chance node that leave it out share whatever is left of 100% equally. If a chance node's branches don't add up to 100%, the chart is still drawn and a warning says so.

type.description: Optional node type, drawn in the decision-analysis convention: "decision" (a square: the decision maker picks a branch), "chance" (a circle: chance picks a branch, with probabilities) or "outcome" (a triangle: an end point, with an optional payoff). Usually omit it and it is inferred: a node whose branches carry a probability is a chance node, a node with no branches an outcome, anything else a decision.

inputSchema.description: A decision tree drawn left to right: decisions (squares), chance events (circles) and end outcomes (triangles), with branch labels, probabilities, payoffs and rolled-back expected values. Also draws plain yes/no question flowcharts.

credit.description: Shows a small "twominutetoolkit.com" credit under the chart, inside the card. Set false to leave it off (for example when the user asks for no branding).

palette.description: Hex colours: the first marks decisions and the best options, the second chance events, the third end outcomes. Pass the user's brand colours here when they name them. Default: indigo, sky, emerald.

prefix.description: Text before every payoff and expected value, e.g. "$", "€" or "£". Default none.

root.description: The first decision or question, on the left (e.g. "Launch strategy for Atlas" or "Does the laptop power on?"), with its branches nested in `children`. Limits: 5 levels in total including the root, up to 5 branches per node and 40 nodes; extras are dropped with a warning, deepest levels and last-listed nodes first.

showEV.description: Roll back expected values: print "EV" on every decision and chance node, draw each decision's best option in the accent colour and mark the rejected options with a ‖ prune mark. When omitted it is on as soon as the tree has both payoffs and probabilities; set false to hide it, true to show it for decision-only trees with payoffs.

suffix.description: Text after every payoff and expected value, e.g. "m", "k", "bn" or " pts". Default none.

title.description: Heading shown top-left of the chart at 22px bold. Every chart has one title row; an empty string hides it.

width.description: Chart width in pixels (640–2400). Omit it (recommended) and the chart sizes itself to its content with comfortable margins, between 880 and 1280px wide. PNG output renders at 2x.
